first.rationale: Two metrics are declining simultaneously: activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ). Memory_31 and memory_86 both support simplification as a direct lever for both problems—memory_31 showed durable lift in first-week activation via signup field reduction, and memory_86 showed onboarding shortening improved completion and time-to-value. I'm verifying memory_31 (signup simplification on SMB activation) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) because they represent the two highest-leverage competing hypotheses: (1) improve funnel efficiency through reduced friction, or (2) defend market share against competitive pricing. Simplification addresses both the activation and onboarding declines simultaneously and aligns with the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue—it improves product-market fit signals rather than discounting, which carries lower long-term risk. The referral incentive (memory_57) is valuable but targets existing customers; activation_messaging (memory_91) is secondary to fixing the conversion funnel itself; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) requires a different customer segment focus. Verification of memory_31 and memory_73 will clarify whether onboarding friction or pricing pressure is the primary driver of current decline.

final.rationale: Verification confirms memory_31 (signup simplification drove +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue on SMB) and definitively rules out memory_73 (promotional pricing caused -12% retention; acquired cohort failed to renew). Given current context—activation down 6% QoQ, onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—simplification directly addresses both metrics with proven mechanics on the SMB segment where we have real friction data. The promotional pricing option is now disqualified by evidence of cohort degradation. Activation messaging (memory_91) could complement but won't solve the funnel leakage. Enterprise sales assist targets a different segment. Referral incentives depend on healthy activation baseline. Simplification is the highest-confidence, lowest-risk lever: it improves product efficiency without discounting, aligns with sustainable revenue objective, and replicates directly on the segment experiencing measurable decline. Running this experiment at standard scale allows measurement of durability against current QoQ trends.
